report.summary: No universal accepted criteria exist; entrypoints are any explicitly designated launch points (console_scripts, `__main__`, git hooks, config files). Dead code is unreachable from these under a conservative call graph. Numbers are scarce: e.g., Vulture reports precision ~60–80% with heavy false positives from dynamic features. Disagreements center on handling dynamism (eval, decorators, importlib). For Daedalus: combine static import/call graphs with explicit entrypoint registration, parse config files statically where possible, and supplement with dynamic coverage; provide manual overrides fo
risks: Static dead-code detection in Python has high false positives due to reflection, eval, metaclasses, and dynamic imports.
External entrypoints (git hooks, config files) may be missed without manual curation.
Tool-specific heuristics (e.g., Vulture, PyCG) are not standardised and require tuning.
On Windows, path handling and shebang-less entrypoints may complicate identification.
todos: Enumerate all known entrypoints from setup.py/console_scripts, `__main__` modules, git hooks, and explicitly listed config files.
Build a conservative import-based call graph (e.g., via `sys.modules` snapshot or AST analysis) starting from those entrypoints.
Integrate optional dynamic coverage data to recover reachability missed by static analysis.
Implement a dead‑code whitelist mechanism to allow developers to suppress false positives.

handoff.suggestion: Consider adopting PyCG (https://github.com/vitsalis/PyCG) for static call‑graph generation, combined with a custom entrypoint‑discovery layer that parses git hook scripts and project‑specific config files. For dynamic augmentation, use `coverage.py` runs under test suites. Use Vulture with a whitelist to flag candidates, but always verify via the call graph.

name: q13-entrypoint-vs-dead
question: What are the accepted criteria for distinguishing a DEAD module from an ENTRYPOINT module in static analysis, given entrypoints invoked via python -m, console_scripts, git hooks, and external config files that live outside the repository?
